response.rationale: R2 is best supported by the raw imaging spans: a well-circumscribed expansile mixed-density maxillary sinus mass with septal destruction, ethmoid/sphenoid invasion, and extensive skull-base/fossa involvement in a pubescent male. R4's painless bony-hard swelling and ridge expansion are compatible but generic, and its expected imaging pattern (ill-defined ground-glass bony expansion) contrasts with the described well-circumscribed destructive/perforating mass. R1 and R3 lack the decisive sinonasal destructive imaging spans; C1 is a redundant site-restricted version of R2.

rejected.why: Redundant append-only completion of R2; the single span 'occupying the entire left maxillary sinus' is nonspecific and adds no independent raw support beyond R2.

The maxillary ridge and tooth-mobility span suggests an odontogenic process, but odontogenic myxoma is not supported by the well-circumscribed mixed-density sinonasal mass with pterygoid/nasopharyngeal destruction; no imaging spans in its favor.

Cherubism requires bilateral jaw expansion and usually familial/mandibular involvement; the vignette has only unilateral cheek/ridge expansion with no family history, so the raw spans are insufficient.
